symbols.name: \(n\)
symbols.def: Number of observed units.

symbols.name: \(k\)
symbols.def: Known number of latent classes, fixed as \(n\) varies.

symbols.name: \(d_x\)
symbols.def: Fixed number of target-proxy coordinates.

symbols.name: \(d_z\)
symbols.def: Fixed number of reference-proxy coordinates.

symbols.name: \(t\)
symbols.def: Generic treatment arm.

symbols.name: \(u\)
symbols.def: Generic latent class.

symbols.name: \(j\)
symbols.def: Generic order of an identifying spectral moment.

symbols.name: \(\alpha\)
symbols.def: Nominal error probability for confidence sets.

symbols.name: \(\eta\)
symbols.def: Generic error probability in a high-probability risk bound.

symbols.name: \(L\)
symbols.def: Common fixed envelope for the VMW observable moment contributions.

symbols.name: \(\pi_0\)
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound on every joint latent-class and treatment-arm probability.

symbols.name: \(\sigma_0\)
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound on the smallest signal singular values.

symbols.name: \(C_0\)
symbols.def: A fixed constant depending only on \(k,d_x,d_z,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).

symbols.name: \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}\)
symbols.def: A finite Lipschitz constant delivered by the primary gap-free positive-measure modulus theorem for the uniformly conditioned causal VMW submodel.

symbols.name: \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\)
symbols.def: A sufficiently small fixed universal constant.

symbols.name: \(c\)
symbols.def: Generic constant in the displayed minimax lower bounds.

symbols.name: \(C\)
symbols.def: Generic finite constant depending only on the fixed model-class parameters displayed in each statement.

symbols.name: \(g\)
symbols.def: Local nearest-neighbor separation used to index labeled-coordinate risk.

symbols.name: \(h\)
symbols.def: Generic scalar displacement along a factorization-preserving local path.

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon\)
symbols.def: Half-separation in the explicit two-class witness.

symbols.name: \(T\)
symbols.def: Observed treatment assignment.

symbols.name: \(U\)
symbols.def: Unobserved finite latent class.

symbols.name: \(X\)
symbols.def: Observed target-proxy feature vector.

symbols.name: \(e_1\)
symbols.def: First canonical basis vector in the target-proxy feature space.

symbols.name: \(Z\)
symbols.def: Observed reference-proxy feature vector.

symbols.name: \(Y(t)\)
symbols.def: Potential outcome under treatment arm \(t\).

symbols.name: \(Y\)
symbols.def: Observed outcome.

symbols.name: \(P\)
symbols.def: Law of one full-data unit.

symbols.name: \(P_O\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the space of \(O\)
symbols.def: Observed margin of \(P\) under the map to \(O=(T,X,Z,Y)\).

symbols.name: \(Q_P^{(n)}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the \(n\)-fold observed-data space
symbols.def: \(Q_P^{(n)}:=P_O^{\otimes n}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal E_n\)
symbols.def: Experiment defined in \(\mathrm{def:sample\text{-}experiment}\).

symbols.name: \(A_t\)
symbols.def: \(A_t(:,u):=E_P[Z\mid U=u,T=t]\).

symbols.name: \(M_t(P)\)
symbols.def: \(M_t(P):=E_{P_O}[ZX^\top\mid T=t]\).

symbols.name: \(N_t(P)\)
symbols.def: \(N_t(P):=E_{P_O}[ZX^\top Y\mid T=t]\).

symbols.name: \(d_S\)
symbols.def: \(d_S(s,s')\) is the sum of operator norms of the four matrix differences and the Euclidean norm of the mean difference.

symbols.name: \(V(P)\)
symbols.def: Any orthonormal basis of \(\operatorname{row}[M_0(P);M_1(P)]\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_x}\), where the brackets denote vertical stacking.

symbols.name: \(\Delta Q(P)\)
symbols.def: \(\Delta Q(P):=\{M_1(P)V(P)\}^{\dagger}N_1(P)V(P)-\{M_0(P)V(P)\}^{\dagger}N_0(P)V(P)\).

symbols.name: \(a(P)\)
symbols.def: \(a(P)^\top:=m_X(P)^\top V(P)\).

symbols.name: \(c(P)\)
symbols.def: \(c(P):=V(P)^\top e_1\), where \(e_1\) is the first coordinate vector in \(\mathbb R^{d_x}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal M\)
symbols.def: Class defined in \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\): a quantitatively uniform subclass of the published VMW model that retains VMW Assumption 1 in its armwise form and adds the fixed margins \(\pi_0\) and \(\sigma_0\).  Its uniform latent potential-outcome and effect envelope is derived from the retained proxy rank, observable-envelope, separation, consistency, positivity, and armwise ignorability conditions.

symbols.name: \(\widehat M_{t,n}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat M_{t,n}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Z_iX_i^\top/\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}\); it is the zero matrix when \(N_{t,n}=0\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat N_{t,n}\)
symbols.type: total empirical outcome-weighted proxy moment matrix
symbols.def: \(\widehat N_{t,n}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Y_iZ_iX_i^\top/\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}\); it is the zero matrix when \(N_{t,n}=0\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat m_{X,n}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat m_{X,n}:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat S_n\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat S_n:=(\widehat M_{0,n},\widehat M_{1,n},\widehat N_{0,n},\widehat N_{1,n},\widehat m_{X,n})\); the empty-arm matrices are zero by definition.

symbols.name: \(\mathscr S\)
symbols.space: subsets of the finite-dimensional summary space
symbols.def: \(\mathscr S:=S(\mathcal M)=\{S(P):P\in\mathcal M\}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal K\)
symbols.space: compact subsets of the finite-dimensional summary space
symbols.def: \(\mathcal K:=\overline{\mathscr S}\), with closure under \(d_S\).

symbols.name: \(\Pi\)
symbols.type: Borel nearest-summary selector with empty-class fallback
symbols.space: maps from the finite-dimensional summary space to the same ambient summary space
symbols.def: When \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\), \(\Pi(s)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in\mathcal K}d_S(q,s)\); when \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), \(\Pi(s)=0\).

symbols.name: \(r_{n,\alpha}\)
symbols.def: \(r_{n,\alpha}:=C_0L\sqrt{\log(C_0/\alpha)/n}\), with \(C_0\) depending only on \(k,d_x,d_z,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).

symbols.name: \(E_P\)

symbols.def: Generic estimator quantified over in the quotient-law minimax lower bound.

symbols.name: \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\)
symbols.def: The total estimator defined in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}net\text{-}law\text{-}estimator}\) by nearest search over a deterministic \(n^{-1/2}\)-net of admissible summaries, stable singular-value thresholding, and aggregate spectral-projector masses.

symbols.name: \(\xi\)
symbols.def: Generic atom-floor candidate law used in the computable confidence set and cluster-mass range.

symbols.name: \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\)
symbols.def: The class-dependent constant displayed in \(\mathrm{prop:polynomial\text{-}net\text{-}law\text{-}estimator}\) for the deterministic lattice-estimator bound.

symbols.name: \(\widehat\lambda_n\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat\lambda_n:=\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n}\), where \(\widehat\vartheta_n\) is the first minimizer of the no-advice finite lattice criterion in \(\mathrm{prop:polynomial\text{-}net\text{-}law\text{-}estimator}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}])\)
symbols.def: Laws supported on at most \(k\) distinct points of \([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]\), every distinct atom having mass at least \(m_\star\).

symbols.name: \(R_{n,\alpha}\)
symbols.def: \(R_{n,\alpha}:=C_{\mathrm{lat}}(r_{n,\alpha}+n^{-1/2})\).

symbols.name: \(\rho_{n,\alpha}\)
symbols.def: \(\rho_{n,\alpha}:=R_{n,\alpha}/m_\star\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\)
symbols.def: Connected components obtained after merging repeated atoms of \(\widehat\lambda_n\) and joining distinct support points at distance at most \(4\rho_{n,\alpha}\).

symbols.name: \(K_C(P)\)
symbols.type: true cluster associated with a computable empirical component \(C\)
symbols.def: For \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) constructed from \(\widehat\lambda_n\), \(K_C(P):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}\).

symbols.name: \(K_C(\xi)\)
symbols.type: candidate cluster associated with a computable empirical component \(C\)
symbols.def: For \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), \(K_C(\xi):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\xi):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}\).

symbols.name: \(\Delta_C(P)\)
symbols.type: external gap of an associated true cluster
symbols.def: \(\Delta_C(P):=\inf\{|x-y|:x\in K_C(P),\ y\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\setminus K_C(P)\}\) when both sets are nonempty, and \(+\infty\) when the complement is empty.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}:=\{\xi:W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}\}\) within the atom-floor law class, as represented in \(\mathrm{def:wasserstein\text{-}confidence\text{-}set}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\)
symbols.def: The retained theoretical image confidence set in \(\mathrm{def:wasserstein\text{-}confidence\text{-}set}\), distinct from \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\).

symbols.name: \(I_C\)
symbols.def: The infimum and supremum of \(\xi(K_C(\xi))\) over \(\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\), with the constrained representation in \(\mathrm{def:cluster\text{-}report}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\)
symbols.space: finite collections of support and mass intervals
symbols.def: The report defined from the explicit center and outer confidence set in \(\mathrm{def:cluster\text{-}report}\).

symbols.name: \(a\)
symbols.def: A sufficiently small universal numerical constant fixed in \(\mathrm{thm:published\text{-}vmw\text{-}converse\text{-}transfer}\) so that both product-experiment total-variation bounds are at most \(1/2\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\)
symbols.def: A generic parameter class inside the published structural/finite-regularity VMW model, quantified subject only to containing the explicit quotient witness pair \(\{P_0^{\mathrm{wit}},P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\}\), not the entire local quotient-law neighborhood.

symbols.name: \(P_{g,h}\)
symbols.def: The Bernoulli proxy law constructed by equations (68)--(72) in the proof of \(\mathrm{thm:matching\text{-}local\text{-}lower\text{-}bounds}\), with effect gap \(g\), signed latent-weight displacement \(h\), and \(P_{g,0}=P_{g/2}^{\mathrm{wit}}\).

symbols.name: \(h(n,g)\)
symbols.def: \(h(n,g):=a\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\}\), the admissible positive orientation of the factorization-preserving path.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}\)
symbols.def: A generic gap-indexed parameter class inside the published VMW model, quantified subject only to containing the explicit separated labeled pair \(\{P_{g,0},P_{g,h(n,g)}\}\), not the entire local labeled-weight neighborhood.

standard.name: VMW causal consistency condition in Assumption 1
VMW armwise latent ignorability condition in Assumption 1

novel.justification: This new uniform joint latent-arm margin is satisfied when every latent class has prevalence bounded away from zero and both treatment arms have assignment probabilities bounded away from zero within each class, as in randomized or overlap-restricted latent-stratified cohorts.

This new uniform proxy-conditioning restriction is satisfied by finite proxy dictionaries whose class-conditional mean columns remain quantitatively distinct; it holds on an open neighborhood of the explicit Bernoulli collision witness.

This additional local-regime shell groups laws whose nonzero nearest-effect gap has order \(g\); it is satisfied by separated finite-class laws after choosing the dyadic shell containing their gap and is used only for the labeled-coordinate frontier.

definitions.name: uniformly conditioned causal VMW submodel
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M:=\{P:\ U\in\{1,\ldots,k\},\ T\in\{0,1\},\ X\in\mathbb R^{d_x},\ Z\in\mathbb R^{d_z},\ Y(0),Y(1),Y\in\mathbb R,\text{ and }P\text{ satisfies each of }\mathrm{ass:reference\text{-}proxy\text{-}separation},\mathrm{ass:target\text{-}proxy\text{-}separation},\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:latent\text{-}ignorability},\mathrm{ass:anchor},\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}x},\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}proxy\text{-}product},\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}outcome\text{-}proxy\text{-}product},\mathrm{ass:latent\text{-}arm\text{-}positivity},\mathrm{ass:proxy\text{-}rank\text{-}margin}\}\).

definitions.name: total Borel empirical observable summary
definitions.construction: For \(N_{t,n}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}\), set \(\widehat M_{t,n}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Z_iX_i^\top/\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}\), \(\widehat N_{t,n}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Y_iZ_iX_i^\top/\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}\), \(\widehat m_{X,n}:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i\), and \(\widehat S_n:=(\widehat M_{0,n},\widehat M_{1,n},\widehat N_{0,n},\widehat N_{1,n},\widehat m_{X,n})\). Both armwise matrices are the zero matrix on \(\{N_{t,n}=0\}\), so \(\widehat S_n\) is a total Borel function of the sample.

definitions.name: compressed effect operator and anchor pair
definitions.construction: Choose any \(V(P)\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\) with orthonormal columns spanning \(\operatorname{row}[M_0(P);M_1(P)]\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_x}\), where the brackets denote vertical stacking, set \(\Delta Q(P):=\{M_1(P)V(P)\}^{\dagger}N_1(P)V(P)-\{M_0(P)V(P)\}^{\dagger}N_0(P)V(P)\), \(a(P)^\top:=m_X(P)^\top V(P)\), and \(c(P):=V(P)^\top e_1\).

definitions.name: quotient latent-effect law
definitions.construction: \(\nu_P:=\sum_{u=1}^{k}p_u\delta_{\tau_u}\), interpreted as a probability measure so that coincident values of \(\tau_u\) carry their aggregate mass.

definitions.name: Borel nearest-summary positive-law repair
definitions.construction:
If \(\mathcal K
e\varnothing\), let \(\overline F:\mathcal K	o\mathcal P_k([-L_{	au},L_{	au}])\) be the unique continuous extension of \(F\) delivered by \(\mathrm{thm:gap	ext{-}free	ext{-}positive	ext{-}measure	ext{-}modulus}\), use the measurable-selection theorem for extrema of Brown and Purves (1973) to fix a Borel selector \(\Pi(s)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in\mathcal K}d_S(q,s)\), and set \(\widehat
u_n:=\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n))\). If \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), set \(\Pi(s):=0\) in the ambient summary space and \(\widehat

definitions.name: theoretical summary-inversion and computable outer Wasserstein confidence sets
definitions.construction:
Retain the original exact summary-inversion set
\[
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}:=
\{\overline F(q):q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n))\le2r_{n,\alpha}\}
\]
when \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\), with \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}:=\{\delta_0\}\) otherwise.  This is the theoretical image set; no computational representation of \(\mathcal K\) or \(\overline F\) is asserted.

For the explicit lattice estimator define
\[
m_\star:=\pi_0,
\qquad R_{n,\alpha}:=C_{\mathrm{lat}}(r_{n,\alpha}+n^{-1/2}),
\]
let \(\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}])\) be the laws on \([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]\) having at most \(k\) distinct atoms, each of mass at least \(m_\star\), and set
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}:=
\{\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]):
W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
This set has the following finite-dimensional constrained-program representation.  Merge repeated atoms of the computed center and write
\(\widehat\lambda_n=\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\widehat w_b\delta_{\widehat x_b}\), where
\(-L_{\tau}\le\widehat x_1<\cdots<\widehat x_{\widehat r}\le L_{\tau}\) and \(1\le\widehat r\le k\).  Then \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) is the union over \(1\le r\le k\) of the laws \(\sum_{a=1}^rw_a\delta_{x_a}\) for which there are variables
\(x_1<\cdots<x_r\), \(w_a\), and \(\gamma_{ab}\) satisfying
\[
\begin{gathered}
-L_{\tau}\le x_1<\cdots<x_r\le L_{\tau},
\qquad w_a\ge m_\star,
\qquad \sum_{a=1}^rw_a=1,\\
\gamma_{ab}\ge0,
\qquad \sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\gamma_{ab}=w_a,
\qquad \sum_{a=1}^{r}\gamma_{ab}=\widehat w_b,
\qquad \sum_{a=1}^{r}\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}
\gamma_{ab}|x_a-\widehat x_b|\le R_{n,\alpha}.
\end{gathered}
\]
Thus \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) is an evaluable fixed-dimensional finite union of ordered-support, weight, and transport-plan constraint sets.  No equality or inclusion relation between \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) and the original \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) is asserted.

definitions.name: computable cluster-adaptive support and mass report
definitions.construction:
Set \(E_P:=\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))\le r_{n,\alpha}\}\) and
\(\rho_{n,\alpha}:=R_{n,\alpha}/m_\star\).  Merge repeated atoms of \(\widehat\lambda_n\), join two distinct support points when their distance is at most \(4\rho_{n,\alpha}\), and let \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) be the resulting connected components.  For \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), define
\[
K_C(P):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\},
\qquad
K_C(\xi):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\xi):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
Rebase the mass interval on the computable outer confidence set:
\[
I_C:=\left[
\inf_{\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi)),
\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi))
\right].
\]
In the ordered-support and transport-plan representation of \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\), both endpoints are values of the same finite union of fixed-dimensional mixed-integer constrained programs: for each \(1\le r\le k\), add variables \(z_a\in\{0,1\}\), impose
\[
z_a=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\min_{c\in C}|x_a-c|\le\rho_{n,\alpha},
\]
and respectively minimize or maximize \(\sum_{a=1}^rw_az_a\) subject to all ordered-support, atom-floor, simplex, and transport constraints in \(\mathrm{def:wasserstein\text{-}confidence\text{-}set}\).  Infimum and supremum are used so that atoms lying exactly on an association boundary are handled by the displayed weak inequality; no claim of an efficient exact solver is made.

The report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) contains, for every component \(C\), the support interval
\([\min C-\rho_{n,\alpha},\max C+\rho_{n,\alpha}]\) and the mass interval \(I_C\).  Finally define
\[
\Delta_C(P):=\inf\{|x-y|:x\in K_C(P),\ y\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\setminus K_C(P)\},
\]
with value \(+\infty\) when the complement is empty.

definitions.name: positive-law ordered-weight estimator
definitions.construction: Write the positive law estimator uniquely as \(\widehat\nu_n=\sum_{\ell=1}^{\widehat s_n}\widehat w_{\ell,n}\delta_{\widehat\tau_{\ell,n}}\), where \(\widehat\tau_{1,n}<\cdots<\widehat\tau_{\widehat s_n,n}\) and every \(\widehat w_{\ell,n}>0\). If \(\widehat s_n=k\), set \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}:=(\widehat w_{1,n},\ldots,\widehat w_{k,n})\); if \(\widehat s_n<k\), set \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}:=(1/k,\ldots,1/k)\). Ordering the finitely many support points and extracting their jump sizes are Borel operations, so this defines a total Borel map into \(\Delta^{k-1}\) without an undeclared dependence on \(\alpha\).

definitions.name: full-rank two-class collision witness
definitions.construction: For \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), let \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) satisfy \(P(U=1)=0.4\), \(P(U=2)=0.6\), \(P(T=1\mid U=1)=0.4\), \(P(T=1\mid U=2)=0.6\), \(X=(1,X_2)^\top\), \(Z=(1,Z_2)^\top\), \(B=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\0.2&0.8\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(A_0=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\0.3&0.7\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(A_1=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\0.35&0.75\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(E[Y(0)\mid U]=(0.25,0.25)\), and \(E[Y(1)\mid U]=(0.5-\varepsilon,0.5+\varepsilon)\). Conditional on \(U\), draw \(X_2,Y(0),Y(1),T\) mutually independently as Bernoulli variables with the stated conditional means; conditional on \(U,T\), draw \(Z_2\) independently of \((X_2,Y(0),Y(1))\) with mean given by \(A_T\), and set \(Y=Y(T)\).

definitions.name: aggregate-projector, positive-moment, and local-score handle
definitions.construction: For positive-law repair, start from Bauer--Fike localization of the empirical compressed operator, replace individual eigenvectors inside overlapping discs by Kato contour projectors, transport aggregate projector mass only across each cluster diameter, and project the finite summary onto the positive \(k\)-atomic moment cone before extracting a real probability measure. For the labeled-weight converse, differentiate the Bernoulli factorization of \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and solve the linear score-cancellation equations for proxy and treatment primitives so that a weight displacement \(h\) preserves the factorization while the observed score has order \(g h\).

definitions.name: fixed-dimensional finite-net positive-law estimator
definitions.construction:
Let \(D:=4d_zd_x+d_x\), \(b:=4\sqrt{d_zd_x}+\sqrt{d_x}\), and \(\epsilon_n:=n^{-1/2}\).  Partition the coordinate box \([-L,L]^D\) into a deterministic lexicographically ordered grid of half-open cubes of side at most \(\epsilon_n/b\).  If \(\mathscr S\ne\varnothing\), from every cube meeting \(\mathscr S\) fix one representative \(q_{n,\ell}\in\mathscr S\), and let \(\widehat q_n\) be the smallest-index minimizer of \(d_S(q_{n,\ell},\widehat S_n)\).  At \(\widehat q_n\), retain the \(k\) right singular directions of the vertically stacked proxy moment whose singular values exceed \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\), call the resulting basis \(V\), and form the compressed effect operator \(\Delta\), left anchor \(a\), and right anchor \(c\) by the formulas in \(\mathrm{def:compressed\text{-}operator}\).  For each distinct eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(\Delta\), put \(E_\lambda:=\prod_{\gamma\ne\lambda}(\Delta-\gamma I_k)/(\lambda-\gamma)\), with the empty product equal to \(I_k\), and define
\[
\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}:=\sum_{\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\Delta)}a^\top E_\lambda c\,\delta_\lambda.
\]
If \(\mathscr S=\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\) to be the unit point mass at zero.

statements.statement:
Every \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfies, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(T=t)&\ge k\pi_0,\\
M_t(P)&=A_t\operatorname{diag}\{P(U=u\mid T=t):1\le u\le k\}B^\top,\\
\sigma_k\{M_t(P)V(P)\}&=\sigma_k\{M_t(P)\}\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\\
\sigma_k\!\left(\begin{bmatrix}M_0(P)\\M_1(P)\end{bmatrix}\right)&\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2,
\end{aligned}
\qquad
\lVert M_t(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},\ \lVert N_t(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},\ \lVert m_X(P)\rVert_2\le L.
\]
Define \(L_{\tau}:=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\).  The retained assumptions further imply, for every \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
|Y(t)|\le L_{\tau}/2\quad P\text{-almost surely conditional on }U=u,
\qquad |\mu_{tu}|\le L_{\tau}/2,
\qquad |\tau_u|\le L_{\tau}.
\]
With the fixed dimensions and anchor normalization, \(\mathcal M\) is a quantitatively uniform conditional-moment subclass of the published VMW parameter class.  It retains VMW Assumption 1 in its exact armwise form, including \(Y(t)\perp T\mid U\) separately for each \(t\), and strengthens the published qualitative latent positivity and full-rank requirements to the fixed margins \(\pi_0\) and \(\sigma_0\).  It imposes no additional latent conditional-moment or potential-outcome support assumption: the displayed potential-outcome envelope is derived from proxy rank, the observable envelopes, reference-proxy separation, consistency, armwise ignorability, and latent--arm positivity.  The converse inclusion and all upper, confidence, cluster, and full-class matching conclusions on the full published VMW class are not asserted; only lower bounds carried by explicit witness paths transfer upward to containing classes.
statements.justification: This proposition derives the exact arm, compressed, stacked, and observable bounds and proves the uniform potential-outcome and effect envelope from retained hypotheses.
statements.gap: VMW uses qualitative rank and positivity.  The present class strengthens those two conditions quantitatively; no extra latent conditional-moment or potential-outcome support condition is imposed.
statements.consumer: The derived envelope supplies the common law support for every estimator and inference result while preserving the one-way subclass and lower-bound-transfer boundaries.

statements.statement: The admissible summary image \(\mathscr S=S(\mathcal M)\) is uniformly bounded under \(d_S\). Hence its closure \(\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S}\) is a compact subset of the finite-dimensional summary space. Moreover, \(\mathcal K\) is nonempty if and only if \(\mathcal M\) is nonempty.
statements.justification: Compactness makes nearest-summary projection exist whenever the statistical model is nonempty, while the explicit empty-class fallback makes the estimator total for incompatible constants.
statements.gap: VMW works with admissible population moments but does not formulate the compact summary closure or the empty-class edge case needed for a total repair through collision.
statements.consumer: The compact domain supports measurable nearest-point selection and the corrected confidence-set construction.

statements.statement: There is a finite \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) such that, for every \(P,P'\in\mathcal M\), \[W_1(\nu_P,\nu_{P'})\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}d_S(S(P),S(P')).\] Equivalently, \(F\) is \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}\)-Lipschitz on \(\mathscr S\) and has a unique extension \(\overline F:\mathcal K\to\mathcal P_k([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}])\) satisfying \[W_1(\overline F(q),\overline F(q'))\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}d_S(q,q'),\qquad q,q'\in\mathcal K.\] The bound is uniform over every multiplicity pattern and simultaneous support merge or split, contains no inverse power of \(\delta(P)\) or \(\delta(P')\), and the extension always returns a positive real probability measure, including after projection of an empirical summary whose raw compressed operator has nonreal eigenvalues.
statements.justification: This gap-free positive-measure modulus is the primary theorem and the sole stability input for the law-level statistical consequences.
statements.gap: Virk, Mazaheri, and Wu (2026, Section 7.1 and Theorem 7.2) provide observable-moment concentration, support localization, and separated inverse-gap weight recovery; they do not provide positive quotient-law stability through multiplicity.
statements.consumer: The theorem converts any valid observable-summary uncertainty region into collision-robust estimation and inference for the quotient effect law.

statements.statement:
If \(\mathcal K
e\varnothing\), a Borel nearest-point selector \(\Pi(s)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in\mathcal K}d_S(q,s)\) exists by Brown and Purves (1973), and \(\widehat
u_n=\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n))\). If \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), the corrected fallback definitions set \(\Pi(s)=0\), \(\widehat
u_n=\delta_0\), and \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}=\{\delta_0\}\). Consequently, in either case \(\widehat
u_n\) is a total Borel positive real law-valued estimator and \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) is nonempty on every sample.
statements.justification: This proposition discharges totality, measurability, positivity, and nonemptiness, including incompatible class-constant choices.
statements.gap: The published spectral estimator does not give a Borel law-valued map on empty arms, nonreal spectra, or an empty admissible-summary class.
statements.consumer: All finite-sample risk, coverage, and cluster-report statements can quantify over every observed sample.

statements.statement:
The explicit sample-evaluable lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) and the theoretical nearest-summary estimator \(\widehat\nu_n=\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n))\) both estimate the quotient law at a collision-uniform root-\(n\) rate.  Specifically, there is a finite \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) such that, for every \(0<\eta<1/2\),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{
\max\{W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P),W_1(\widehat\nu_n,\nu_P)\}
>C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}\right\}\le\eta.
\]
Both estimators are total, Borel, positive, and real-law-valued on every sample.  The first is computable by the explicit no-advice finite lattice in \(\mathrm{prop:polynomial\text{-}net\text{-}law\text{-}estimator}\); the second remains the closure-based theoretical construction used for statements requiring membership in \(\overline F(\mathcal K)\).  The simultaneous bound includes \(\{N_{t,n}=0\}\), whose probability is at most \((1-k\pi_0)^n\) for each arm, and is uniform over every effect multiplicity pattern.
statements.justification: This gives collision-uniform root-\(n\) estimation for both the explicit computable law estimator and the retained theoretical closure estimator.
statements.gap: Published VMW recovery uses separated eigenvectors for masses; neither estimator here incurs an inverse effect gap, but the result remains confined to the stated uniformly conditioned subclass.
statements.consumer: Conditional on a separate censoring and prespecified finite-fitness bridge, the explicit law estimator could support stable heterogeneity summaries for the 504-patient stage-III NSCLC PROTECT setting; the theorem does not validate that bridge.

statements.statement:
For a suitable choice of the simultaneous-concentration constant in \(r_{n,\alpha}\), both the original summary-inversion set and the computable outer set are honest:
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}\{
\nu_P\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\}
\ge1-\alpha.
\]
Both sets are nonempty on every sample, and
\[
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})
\le4C_{\mathrm{mod}}r_{n,\alpha},
\qquad
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha})
\le2R_{n,\alpha}.
\]
The second set has the explicit fixed-dimensional constrained-program representation in \(\mathrm{def:wasserstein\text{-}confidence\text{-}set}\).  Coverage and root-\(n\) \(W_1\)-diameter are uniform over every collision, merge, and split stratum; neither equality nor inclusion between the two confidence sets is claimed.
statements.justification: The theorem now gives simultaneous honest root-\(n\)-diameter inference for the retained theoretical set and an explicit computable outer set.
statements.gap: Existing Wasserstein confidence-set theory does not provide this collision-uniform proxy-law construction or its atom-floor constrained representation.
statements.consumer: The computable outer set supports aggregate latent-effect-law reporting without conditioning on a preliminary separation decision.

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), on \(E_P\), the sets \(K_C(P)\), indexed by \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) constructed from \(\widehat\lambda_n\), form a partition of \(\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\).  Every \(K_C(P)\) lies in the reported support interval for \(C\), and \(I_C\), computed over \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\), contains \(\nu_P(K_C(P))\).  More explicitly, a singleton associated cluster has support-interval length at most
\[
4\rho_{n,\alpha}=4R_{n,\alpha}/m_\star,
\]
its mass interval has length at most
\[
\frac{8}{m_\star}\min\!\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\delta(P)}\right\},
\]
and every associated cluster satisfies
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_C)
\le\frac{8}{m_\star}\min\!\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\Delta_C(P)}\right\},
\]
where the right side is interpreted as zero when \(\Delta_C(P)=+\infty\).  Finally,
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}(E_P)\ge1-\alpha.
\]
Thus the entire report has a fixed-dimensional constrained-program representation, while effects unresolved at the \(\rho_{n,\alpha}\) scale are pooled without hiding the true-cluster association or its external gap.
statements.justification: This turns the computable outer law set into an honest multiplicity-aware support and aggregate-mass report with explicit transport constants.
statements.gap: Existing adaptive Wasserstein confidence-set results do not translate weak-metric coverage into computable multiplicity-aware support and mass reports for this nonnormal causal operator.
statements.consumer: The report tells applied analysts when separate latent-effect coordinates are supportable and when only a pooled cluster statement is honest.

statements.statement: As a labeled-coordinate consequence of the root-law estimator and the additional gap-local regime, there is a finite \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) such that, uniformly over \(g\in(0,1/4]\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(g)}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\lVert\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}-p^{\uparrow}(P)\rVert_1\right]\le C\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.\] The inverse-gap behavior concerns ordered labels and does not enter the \(W_1\) risk of \(\nu_P\).
statements.justification: This consequence isolates the instability induced by scientific insistence on effect-ordered labels.
statements.gap: Virk, Mazaheri, and Wu (2026, Theorem 7.2) already supply separated inverse-gap weight recovery; the new content sought here is uniform transition accounting together with the matching factorization-preserving local lower bound.
statements.consumer: The bound supplies an explicit reporting threshold for separate latent-stratum weights.

statements.statement: For every \(0\le\varepsilon\le1/8\), with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\), the law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\). It satisfies \(P(T=0)=0.48\), \(P(T=1)=0.52\), \(\det(B)=0.6\), \(\det(A_0)=\det(A_1)=0.4\), \(\det(M_0(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))=0.06\), \(\det(M_1(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))=0.4\cdot0.6\cdot36/169\), and \(\nu_{P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}}=0.4\delta_{0.25-\varepsilon}+0.6\delta_{0.25+\varepsilon}\). At \(\varepsilon=0\), all proxy matrices remain nonsingular, the quotient law is \(\delta_{0.25}\), and the latent weights remain unequal.
statements.justification: The explicit interior witness rules out an apparent collision phenomenon caused by collapsing proxy rank or treatment positivity.
statements.gap: The VMW paper does not provide this unequal-weight, exact-effect-collision submodel; the proposition is a construction check rather than a stand-alone statistical advance.
statements.consumer: The witness is the early kill test for the modulus and the common base point for both local lower-bound regimes.

statements.statement:
For the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\), there are \(c,C>0\) such that \[\inf_{\widetilde
u_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal L_n^{
u}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[W_1(\widetilde
u_n,
u_P)]\ge rac{c}{\sqrt n}\] and, uniformly for \(g\in(0,1/4]\), \[\inf_{\widetilde p_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal L_{n,g}^{p}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\lVert\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)Vert_1]\ge c\min\left\{1, rac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}ight\}.\] Each inequality is certified by an explicit two-point path inside the displayed Bernoulli proxy factorization. The quotient-law path has one-observation Kullback--Leibler divergence at most \(C/n\) and \(W_1\)-separation at least \(c/\sqrt n\). For the labeled path, a weight displacement \(h\) preserves both proxy conditional-independence factorizations, positivity, and rank, has one-observation observed-data Kullback--Leibler divergence at most \(C g^2h^2\), and has ordered-weight separation at least \(c|h|\); taking \(|h|=c\min\{1,(\sqrt n g)^{-1}\}\) gives the second bound.
statements.justification: The verified factorization-preserving paths distinguish quotient-law regularity from labeled-coordinate irregularity in the actual observed proxy experiment.
statements.gap: Ordinary-mixture collision lower bounds do not preserve the VMW proxy factorization and therefore do not establish the observed-data Kullback--Leibler order required here.
statements.consumer: The converse calibrates both the smallest possible law-level radius and the separation needed for defensible labeled-weight reporting.

statements.statement:
For the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\), the upper and lower bounds on the same uniformly conditioned causal VMW class imply that, for finite \(0<c<C<\infty\),
\[
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}\le\inf_{\widetilde\nu_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[W_1(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P)]\le\frac{C}{\sqrt n}.
\]
statements.justification: This corollary states the immediate same-class minimax frontier on the explicit parameter class containing the local experiment.
statements.gap: VMW does not state a quotient-law minimax risk through collisions on this uniformly conditioned causal submodel.
statements.consumer: The equality of upper and lower orders calibrates the smallest uniform Wasserstein accuracy on the displayed experiment.

statements.statement:
For the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\), uniformly for \(g\in(0,1/4]\), the labeled upper and lower bounds on the same gap stratum imply that, for finite \(0<c<C<\infty\),
\[
c\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}\le\inf_{\widetilde p_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(g)}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\lVert\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\rVert_1]\le C\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]
statements.justification: This corollary makes the clipped inverse-gap rate a same-class minimax statement on the explicit parameter class containing the local path.
statements.gap: VMW supplies separated recovery but not the factorization-preserving local converse that certifies the transition rate on the displayed class.
statements.consumer: The frontier gives analysts a sharp threshold for when separate effect-ordered masses are statistically defensible.

statements.justification: This isolates exact or sharp computation of the original theoretical image after explicit law estimation and an evaluable honest report have been constructed.
statements.gap: The core does not give an exact finite representation of the admissible-summary closure and extension image, nor an exact polynomial-time algorithm for its support-dependent extrema.
statements.consumer: A solution would reproduce the original sharp summary-inversion image and its exact extrema; no additional evaluable outer confidence set is needed.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from the uniformly conditioned causal fixed-\(k\) VMW submodel.
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(T_i,X_i,Z_i,Y_i)\), for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), are independent with common observed law \(P_O\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with every joint latent-class and arm probability bounded below by \(\pi_0\).
sampling_model.overlap: Uniform latent-arm positivity and uniform proxy singular-value margins are imposed; no treatment-effect eigengap is imposed for law-level results, while the additional \(g\)-window is used only for labeled-coordinate statements.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The published VMW boundedness conditions are imposed separately on \(X\), \(ZX^\top\), and \(YZX^\top\). Armwise empirical moments divide by \(\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}\), are zero on empty arms, and combine with \(n^{-1}\sum_iX_i\) to form the total Borel summary \(\widehat S_n\), followed by Borel nearest-summary projection into \(\mathcal K\) and the continuous positive-law extension \(\overline F\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The published structural/finite-regularity model imposes the two proxy conditional independences, causal consistency, armwise latent ignorability, qualitative proxy rank, and strict positivity, but not the fixed quantitative margins used here.  The explicit quotient pair satisfies those base conditions even though its collision point is outside the separated simple-effect recovery class of Theorem 7.2; the labeled pair is separated.

Theorem 5.4 identifies every polynomial latent-effect moment, while Section 7.1 and Theorem 7.2 localize roots and recover weights under separated simple effects with inverse nearest-eigengap dependence; they do not provide the collision-uniform positive-law modulus proved here.
Projection of noisy summaries onto a feasible truncated-moment space guarantees a positive finite mixing measure and yields Wasserstein rates for Gaussian mixture deconvolution.
Around an \(m_0\)-component ordinary mixture fitted with \(m\) components, the local minimax Wasserstein rate is \(n^{-1/(4(m-m_0)+2)}\), whereas pointwise root-\(n\) behavior can occur.
Necessary and sufficient testing-versus-estimation conditions govern honest adaptive Wasserstein confidence sets over density-smoothness classes.
Honest confidence regions may be centered at adaptive estimators, with achievable diameter controlled jointly by estimation and testing rates.
Data-driven inference for Wasserstein distance between topic-model mixing measures handles nonsmooth transport geometry and supplies asymptotically valid confidence intervals for that distance.

tldr: On a uniformly conditioned causal VMW submodel, the primary theorem is a gap-free Lipschitz modulus from the observable moment summary to the positive quotient latent-effect law in \(W_1\), uniform through simultaneous effect merges and splits. Root-\(n\) estimation, honest root-\(n\)-diameter confidence sets, and a cluster report with explicit true-cluster association follow from that modulus. Same-class minimax corollaries give root-\(n\) quotient-law risk and effect-ordered weight risk \(\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,\delta)^{-1}\}\), using factorization-preserving paths on an explicit full-rank unequal-weight two-class witness. VMW supplies population moment identification and separated inverse-gap recovery; the proposed results concern gap-free positive quotient-law stability under the stated additional uniform conditions, not the full VMW class.

project_justification.gap: Virk, Mazaheri, and Wu identify the operator moments and obtain separated eigenpair recovery, but their finite-sample analysis does not provide a gap-free map from an observable summary to a positive real quotient law when isolation discs overlap or empirical eigenvalues are nonreal.
project_justification.niche: The regular object can be the quotient probability law that aggregates mass at equal effects, even though effect-ordered latent weights become irregular near a collision.
project_justification.fill: The paper makes the positive-measure \(W_1\) modulus the root theorem on a uniformly conditioned causal VMW submodel, derives total root-\(n\) estimation, honest root-\(n\)-diameter sets and well-posed cluster reports, and calibrates same-class quotient-law and labeled-weight minimax risk using observed-Kullback--Leibler paths that preserve the proxy factorization.

related_work: Virk, Mazaheri, and Wu (2026, Theorem 5.4, Proposition 6.2, Section 7.1, and Theorem 7.2) provide the population operator-moment identity, the known homogeneity reduction, bounded observable-moment conditions, support localization, and separated inverse-eigengap weight recovery. The proposed theorem targets gap-free positive quotient-law stability on the explicitly narrower uniformly conditioned causal submodel; the observed-margin inclusion proposition derives the relevant VMW observable margins in one direction, without claiming the converse or resolution of the full VMW class. Mazaheri, Squires, and Uhler (2025) identify a finite latent-effect mixture through scalar synthetic moments and a Hankel pencil, without collision-uniform inference. Bauer and Fike (1960) localize spectra of perturbed diagonalizable operators, while Kato (1995, Chapter II) supplies contour-defined aggregate projectors for externally isolated clusters; neither result assigns positive causal spectral masses through a merge. Wu and Yang (2020, Sections 1, 4, and 5) project noisy summaries onto a feasible moment space before positive atomic extraction in Gaussian mixture deconvolution and inform the repair handle. Heinrich and Kahn (2018, Sections 3--5) and Ho and Nguyen (2016) analyze collision singularities for ordinary mixtures, not factorization-preserving paths in the VMW observed proxy experiment. Deo and Randrianarisoa (2023), Robins and van der Vaart (2006), and Bing, Bunea, and Niles-Weed (2025) inform the confidence-set architecture but do not treat multiplicity of a nonnormal causal operator. Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2018) motivate proxy conditional-independence and rank discipline. Van Amsterdam et al. (2022) provide the PROTECT stage-III NSCLC consumer, conditional on a separate finite-fitness and censoring bridge; their hazard model is not claimed to lie in \(\mathcal M\). Brown and Purves (1973) supply the measurable-extrema selection theorem used to choose a Borel nearest point in the compact feasible-summary closure.
technical_internal_limitation: The root theorem still requires a uniform operator-to-positive-measure perturbation argument through simultaneous merges and splits. Compact-summary projection and the continuous extension make the estimator total and Borel, but may be computationally expensive; the open question asks for a basis-invariant constructive replacement when the raw empirical spectrum is nonreal. The lower-bound work must display the factorization-preserving tangent, verify all class restrictions along it, and calculate the one-observation observed-data Kullback--Leibler orders \(O(n^{-1})\) and \(O(g^2h^2)\). The early kill test is the full root-\(n\) moment-perturbation cone around \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\): any admissible pair with summary distance of root-\(n\) order but quotient-law distance larger than root-\(n\) order invalidates the kernel.
honest_scope: The law-level theorems fix and know \(k,d_x,d_z\), use the exact VMW observable conditional independences, and impose two explicitly new uniform-conditioning conditions: a lower bound on every joint latent-arm probability and singular-value margins for \(A_0,A_1,B\). These conditions imply \(P(T=t)\ge k\pi_0\) and, under the conditional normalization of \(M_t(P)\), \(\sigma_k(M_t(P))\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2\); the converse inclusion and gap-free resolution of the full VMW class are not claimed. Compact potential-outcome support is an additional causal restriction, while the VMW bounds on \(X\), \(ZX^\top\), and \(YZX^\top\) are stated separately. The two-sided \(g\)-window is an additional local-regime shell used only for labeled weights. Population identification and the homogeneous identities \(\Delta Q(P)=\tau_\star I_k\) and \(\nu_P=\delta_{\tau_\star}\) are published VMW background. Recovery of latent labels at equality, unknown \(k\), and a polynomial-time total repair remain outside the settled scope. PROTECT remains a conditional consumer until a separate theorem maps a prespecified finite fitness stratification and bounded censoring-adjusted outcome into the VMW moment model.
